figures.alt: Commercial preconstruction table with abstract plans, measuring tools, blank clipboard, and coordination materials
figures.caption: A change can be priced quickly when the original scope, affected drawings, assumptions, labor, material, and equipment are organized before the field condition turns into rework.

figures.alt: Contractor qualification binder beside blank insurance documentation and a project notebook
figures.caption: Clear scope language and written records make it possible to distinguish added work from the original commitment. Good documentation protects both the GC and the trade partner.
figures.before: Use Scope Language That Can't Be Misread

figures.alt: Commercial space under selective demolition with retained ceiling grid, opened partition bays, and controlled work areas
figures.caption: Existing conditions can change a field plan. The right response is to document the condition, define the affected scope, and obtain authorization before building beyond the contract.
figures.before: Get the Authorization in Writing Before the Work Begins
